svg.title: Dropout in a transformer encoder: where it sits and why it matters
svg.desc: Top section shows the encoder block with dropout placement. Bottom section shows what dropout does to a tensor and explains why it prevents over-reliance on individual neurons.
svg.text: Part 1. Where dropout sits inside the encoder block
Part 2. What dropout does — example tensor (1×8 slice)
During training, ~10% of values become 0. Surviving values are scaled by 1/(1−p) ≈ 1.11.

g.text: Why dropout sits on sub-layer output, not the residual
The residual x carries the clean, accumulated signal across all 6 layers. Dropping it would
destroy ~50% of the signal by layer 6 (0.9⁶ ≈ 0.53). Worst case with current placement:
a sub-layer contributes nothing this step. x still flows through unbroken.
